MMM.rationale: 3M's Q2 2026 results show a genuine turnaround gaining traction: adjusted EPS of $2.40 beat consensus by 5.7%, organic sales grew 5.4% YoY, and adjusted operating margin expanded to 24.9%. Management raised full-year guidance to $8.80-$8.95 EPS (up from $8.50-$8.70) and increased FCF guidance to $4.7-$4.9B. Safety & Industrial segment revenue rose 8.2% and Transportation & Electronics grew 6.2%, though Consumer remains weak (-1.8%). The balance sheet carries elevated debt (~$12.6B as of Q3 2025) and total equity of only $3.3B, reflecting prior legal settlements. Valuation is stretched: P/E of 32.3x is near the top of its 1-year range (17.7-32.5), and P/B of 27.3x is at the ceiling of its range (17.1-27.5), having expanded sharply from ~18-19x a year ago. The stock has rallied +16.3% over the past quarter to $169.59. While the fundamental trajectory is clearly improving, the current valuation already prices in much of the turnaround, leaving limited upside unless execution continues to exceed expectations. Legal/PFAS risks and tariff exposure ($850M potential annual impact before mitigation) remain overhangs. The Q2 beat and guidance raise provide a near-term positive catalyst, but the elevated multiple caps the attractiveness.
